band_change_evidence_test.explanation: The test fails on the tier requirement. Six independent sources were used — TechCrunch, The Robot Report, TT News, TechTimes, TSG Invest and the company website — which satisfies the two-source part comfortably. None reaches tier 4. Agility Robotics is private, publishes no institutional data and no responsibility report, and no independent audit of it exists. The pending Churchill Capital Corp XI merger will create public reporting obligations but had not done so at the assessment date. The strongest available evidence is tier-3 trade reporting of forward-looking product claims.

key_evidence: Why it matters: Agility Robotics builds a humanoid that does warehouse work, and it publishes nothing about what happens to the workers whose tasks it takes.

Digit version 5 is being built to sense humans and work without a safety fence alongside warehouse staff. That is a genuine worker-safety design commitment and it is the company’s strongest compassion evidence.
Digit works commercial shifts at Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada in Ontario and at a GXO warehouse in Flowery Branch, Georgia, and has moved 100,000 totes at one GXO site.
The IEEE Humanoids 2026 conference has made labour displacement its defining theme. No Agility position on the displacement its own product causes was located.

This assessment supersedes the 2026-07-22 Agility file, which returned 61.9 and recommended CONFIRM. That file cited a single TechCrunch article for all 40 subdimensions and is not a valid 40-subdimension assessment.
